# Scoped Video Match — One Studio or Actor

> Operator request, 2026-08-06: *"It would be great to be able to run a batch video match on a single studio's films or a single actor's films (a new entry in their ellipsis menu). Same function as with the All Videos, but just this focused subset of videos."*
## Why it matters
The run is **rate-limited by the source**, so its cost is proportional to how many videos it walks. Matching a two-thousand-video library to fix one studio's forty is most of an hour of requests to do about a minute of real work — which in practice means the fix does not get done.
## What was built
`VideoBatchMatchModel.Scope` — a label and a set of asset ids. `nil` runs the whole library, which is what Settings still asks for, so the existing entry point is unchanged.
⚠️ **The scope is applied in ONE place**, `assetsInScope(_:)`, which both the pre-count and the crawl call. That file already carries comments recording two separate defects where `total` and the loop disagreed about what was being walked — the progress bar that could never pass halfway, and the total that doubled on a second run. A scope that reached only one of them would have been the third instance of the same bug.
### The entry point
A **Match These N Videos** item in the profile page's ⋯ menu, on both actor and studio pages — the same menu that now carries Rename Globally, Edit Profile and Match with … . Offered only when a video provider is actually installed, per D3: an available but uninstalled plugin gets no affordance anywhere.
⚠️ **Scoped to the videos ON SCREEN (****`filteredAssets`****), not to every video the entity has.** If a filter is narrowing the page, the run follows it. That is the more useful behaviour — it makes any subset matchable, including a studio family view or a single career-arc age — but it means the count is the honest label, not the entity name. Hence **"Match These 40 Videos"** rather than "Match This Studio".
### Saying what it covers
The run screen is otherwise identical to the whole-library one, so a scoped run states its scope before it starts: the title reads **Match These Videos**, and the description leads with *"Matching the 40 videos shown for ‹name›."*
Without that, a screen headed "Match every video" on a page showing forty of two thousand is the kind of wording that gets a run cancelled halfway out of doubt about what it is actually doing.
## Verification
macOS and iOS build; LibraryCore 1,072 tests, 0 failures (unchanged — this is view-model work, and `VideoBatchPolicy` was not touched). D9 clean. SF Symbol verified to resolve rather than assumed.
⚠️ Not run against a populated library. The behaviour worth checking first is the **count**: the progress readout should show the scoped total, not the library total, since that is exactly the class of defect the one-place scoping was written to avoid.
